purpose: Short learner-facing bridge copy in the learner's own/source language. It prepares the learner to compare kinship systems without assuming family words translate one-to-one.
source_summary_en: Family words divide relationships differently across languages. One language may use a broad word where another builds age, gender, family side, marriage, or another relationship detail into the term.
localization_rules: Keep the bridge short: normally two sentences or less.
Use ordinary native-language wording, not anthropological jargon.
Do not claim that one kinship pattern describes every dialect, family, region, religion, or community using the language.
The bridge may mention common distinctions in the source language when well supported, but uncertain lower-resource details should stay general rather than being invented.
These are generated candidates until native-speaker review.
